item.title: Emergency services respond to river incident in King's Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Emergency services respond to river incident in King's Lynn
Emergency crews were called to the River Great Ouse in King's Lynn on Saturday afternoon following reports of a person in the water. The alarm was raised by the local ferry team at 3:04pm. By the time the Hunstanton Coastguard Rescue Team arrived at South Quay, the individual had been recovered from the river and was receiving medical attention from paramedics.
The incident involved a multi-agency response, including the East of England Ambulance Service, Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service, and Norfolk Constabulary. Once the person was confirmed safe, all teams were stood down. The Coastguard is reminding the public to dial 999 and ask for the Coastguard if they spot anyone in difficulty along the coast.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
North Lynn man charged following bus station incident
A 20-year-old man has been charged following an incident at King’s Lynn bus station on Monday evening. Daniel Neves, of Walpole Road, faces two counts of assaulting emergency workers and two charges of criminal damage relating to a police officer’s watch and body-worn camera.
The charges follow an encounter where officers attempted to seize an illegal e-scooter. West Norfolk Police have thanked members of the public for their assistance during the arrest. Mr Neves has been bailed and is due to appear at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on November 12. Police say they are increasing foot patrols at the bus station to address reports of anti-social behaviour as the evenings grow darker.

item.title: West Norfolk Council deputy leader calls for new approach to town centre revival
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk Council deputy leader calls for new approach to town centre revival
West Norfolk Council’s deputy leader, Simon Ring, says the future of King’s Lynn must move beyond retail to succeed. Welcoming a new £210 million government high street regeneration package, Councillor Ring stated that the town needs to adapt to modern habits by creating a mixed-use centre where people live, work, and spend their leisure time.
The council is already working to bring long-term vacant buildings, such as the former Post Office and Debenhams, back into use. Meanwhile, North West Norfolk MP James Wild is supporting a campaign to cut business costs and tackle crime, highlighting concerns from local firms regarding business rates and energy bills. The council is currently awaiting details on how much funding may be allocated to the area.

item.title: Celebrating King’s Lynn’s historic figures
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Celebrating King’s Lynn’s historic figures
King’s Lynn is home to three statues honouring figures who shaped both the town and the wider world. The collection includes a bronze tribute to King John on New Conduit Street, unveiled in 2016 to mark the monarch’s 1204 charter which granted the town its independence.
The town also features a statue of explorer Captain George Vancouver on Purfleet Quay, commemorating his extensive mapping of the Northwest Pacific coastline. Finally, a statue at Guanock Place celebrates Frederick Savage, a renowned engineer and former mayor who became famous for his pioneering work on steam-powered fairground rides. These landmarks serve as a permanent reminder of the town’s rich history and the significant contributions of these three men.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/how-much-do-you-know-about-town-s-three-statues-honouring-ke-9487187/

King’s Lynn Waterstones names Book of the Week
Waterstones in King’s Lynn has selected ‘Craftland: A Journey Through Britain's Living Past’ by James Fox as its current Book of the Week. The publication explores the work of remaining master craftspeople across the country, ranging from wheelwrights to silversmiths. The author examines how traditional trades and vanishing skills have helped shape British national identity and regional culture over hundreds of years.
The store on Norfolk Street has also released its latest top ten list, which includes titles by authors such as Elly Griffiths, Anthony Horowitz, and Sarah Vaughan. Readers can find more information on these selections by visiting the King’s Lynn branch.

King’s Lynn care provider placed in special measures
A King’s Lynn-based home care service, Dedicated Care East Anglia, has been downgraded to "inadequate" by the Care Quality Commission. The watchdog found the provider breached five legal regulations, including those regarding safeguarding and safe care. Inspectors raised concerns over staff using faulty equipment and failing to follow care plans. One report noted a staff member left a distressed client to smoke outside.
The service, based at Tansley Business Park, is now in special measures and will be closely monitored. While the firm expressed disappointment and is challenging some findings, it has appointed external experts to review its processes. The CQC noted that some families reported feeling their relatives were treated with dignity and respect.
